RESULTS — per-group statistics (from main study file, `length` = pages of the original paper; group defined via `project`):

| Group | definition | n rows | n unique papers | mean | median | sd | min | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Experimental Economics | project=='ee' (EERP) | 18 | 18 | **28.00** | **27.5** | 7.37 | 16 | 45 |
| Psychology | project=='rpp' (RPP) | 97 | 95 | **11.22** | **9.0** | 6.30 | 1 | 31 |
| Psychology (sensitivity: 7 drop=True rows excluded) | project=='rpp' | 90 | 88 | 11.00 | 9.0 | 6.16 | 1 | 31 |

Robustness checks (all as agreed):
- Row-vs-paper: for RPP, 97 rows vs 95 unique papers; the 2 duplicate rows are the same paper measured for two effects with identical length, so mean (11.22) and median (9.0) are unchanged either way. EE is 18 rows = 18 papers (1:1).
- `drop`: excluding the 7 rpp `drop=True` rows moves the Psychology mean only 11.22 → 11.00; median unchanged. EE has no dropped rows.
- `aggregated`: NaN for both groups — no multi-lab aggregation to worry about.

Headline numbers: **Experimental Economics (n=18 papers) mean 28.0 pages (median 27.5); Psychology / RPP (n=97 rows, 95 papers) mean 11.2 pages (median 9.0).** Mean difference ≈ 16.8 pages — Experimental Economics original papers are, on average, roughly 17 pages (≈1.5x longer relative to the Psychology group's 11.2) longer than Psychology/RPP original papers.
